Racial callback gaps among 97 large firms

Source: R/data.R
krw_discrimination.Rd

Firm-specific differences in callback rates for applications with distinctively white and distinctively Black names. The original correspondence experiment is from Kline, Rose and Walters (2022). Following their 2024 analysis and the replication code of Walters (2024), firms with at least 40 sampled vacancies and an overall callback rate of at least 3 percent are included: 97 firms, 78,910 applications and 10,453 vacancies. Each firm is one site of the model; the standard errors are clustered by vacancy within firm.

Usage

krw_discrimination

Format

A data frame with 97 rows and 8 columns:

site

Sequential site number, in ascending order of firm_id.

firm_id

Firm identifier in the original data.

firm_name

Name of the firm as supplied in the replication data.

yi

Difference in callback probability, white minus Black, estimated by ordinary least squares. Positive values favor applications with distinctively white names. The values are differences of proportions: multiply by 100 for percentage points.

sei

Standard error of yi, clustered by vacancy, with the CR1 finite-sample correction used by Stata's clustered OLS regression.

vi

Sampling variance, sei^2.

n_jobs

Number of distinct sampled vacancies in the firm.

n_obs

Number of applications in the firm.

Source

Kline, P., Rose, E. K. and Walters, C. R. (2022). Systemic discrimination among large U.S. employers. The Quarterly Journal of Economics, 137(4), 1963-2036. doi:10.1093/qje/qjac024 . The analysis sample follows Kline, P., Rose, E. K. and Walters, C. R. (2024). A discrimination report card. American Economic Review, 114(8), 2472-2525. doi:10.1257/aer.20230700 . Data and regression code were obtained from the replication package accompanying Walters, C. R. (2024). Empirical Bayes methods in labor economics. In Handbook of Labor Economics, 5, 183-260. doi:10.1016/bs.heslab.2024.11.001 . The package is available through https://sites.google.com/view/christopher-walters/research. The Bayesian reanalysis is described in Lee and Sui (2025), doi:10.3390/math13162639 . data-raw/krw-discrimination.R in the source repository reproduces the estimates from krw_data.dta, and the attribute source of the data frame records where the data came from.

See also

as_bef_data(), vignette("bayesEfron")
